rows.title: What’s Working: New broadband laws to help Colorado streamline distribution of $800+ million
rows.standfirst: More internet options for apartment, mobile home park residents could be coming, too. Plus: ACP has ended, 0% interest loans for job trainees and more!

rows.title: Hope Springs in Greeley, the largest Habitat neighborhood in the West, gets a 3D twist and $100M to build 491 homes
rows.standfirst: As median home prices edge beyond $500,000 in Weld County, there’s new hope with this community of affordable housing options

rows.title: Colorado’s growing approach to solving chronic homelessness: Permanent housing with few rules
rows.standfirst: Jefferson Center and WellPower of Denver are building permanent supportive housing complexes modeled after a 2017 Denver building that still has a waitlist

rows.title: Estes Park has growing pains this summer. From construction to elk, here’s how to manage it.
rows.standfirst: Understanding the downtown road re-construction mess, a still-shuttered national park campground and elk attacks are a few of the keys to the area

rows.title: The very last Boulder Techstars class graduates as company ends 17-year run in city
rows.standfirst: The business accelerator program, which helped thousands of tech companies get started, is now based in New York, and has an office in Denver.

rows.title: What’s Working: Why Colorado could start attracting more filmmakers
rows.standfirst: Incentives could also provide steady employment for industry. Plus: What other states like Georgia pay, entrepreneur Polis, around $225 million available in small business loans, more!

rows.title: A car crash devastated a Colorado farming family. Amputation turned it around.
rows.standfirst: Two years ago, Heidi Rohwer was injured in a car crash that killed her mother. After setbacks, pain and uncertainty, amputation has helped her see the bright side again.

rows.title: Coloradans from every political party, age group and region want politicians to do something about the cost of living
rows.standfirst: Voter Voices is a statewide survey asking Coloradans what they want politicians to focus on in the upcoming election. Hundreds of answers reflect a concern with the high cost of living.

rows.title: Developers in the U.S. are forced to build parking no one uses. In Colorado, that’s starting to change.
rows.standfirst: Last month, Gov. Jared Polis signed a new law preventing some cities from requiring minimum levels of parking at multifamily residences built near public transit

rows.title: How a nationwide slowdown in housing sales put a kink in Colorado’s mattress recycling
rows.standfirst: Used mattress foam piling up at Spring Back Colorado’s recycling plant in Commerce City is due to a lack of a market, a problem that recyclers of other materials are wrestling with, too.

rows.title: Xcel’s $440M plan to cut greenhouse gas emissions gets Colorado’s OK — but it could boost utility bills again
rows.standfirst: The Clean Heat Plan seeks to move more Colorado homes and businesses to electricity from natural gas. Some worry the utility could make windfall profits from fighting the climate crisis.

rows.title: Does a Colorado hotline offer to pay callers to house migrants?
rows.standfirst: The Colorado Sun partners with Gigafact to investigate viral claims

rows.title: Governor, lawmakers are already planning big revisions to Colorado’s first-in-the nation artificial intelligence law
rows.standfirst: Jared Polis, Attorney General Phil Weiser and a top Democratic lawmaker agree that Senate Bill 205 needs “additional clarity” and “improvements.” The proclamation follows a letter signed by 200 prominent technology executives and venture capitalists.

rows.title: What’s Working: How a Denver company is fighting the problem of underemployment
rows.standfirst: Students from first-generation families often lack access to networks to help get that first job. GlobalMindED is working on that. Plus: Underemployment rates by state, Denver inflation slows.

rows.title: Southeastern Coloradans could pay $20 more a month if state regulators approve utility’s rate increase
rows.standfirst: Officials in Pueblo and Cañon City are pushing back against Black Hills Energy’s proposal, calling it “one more burden on a poor community”

rows.title: An experiment doled out money to homeless people in Denver, no strings attached. Here’s what happened.

rows.title: Alamo Drafthouse workers hopeful ownership change will favor newly formed union

rows.standfirst: Colorado still has 1.7 open jobs for every unemployed worker. Plus: Hiring frenzy at United Airlines and McDonald’s subsides, a $20M grant for CU’s quantum shop and more!

rows.title: 16th Street Mall reaches tipping point as business frustration grows with delayed renovations
rows.standfirst: What a mess. Delayed construction, a drop in visitors and fewer workers in downtown compound to hammer businesses along iconic Denver mall.

rows.title: Colorado’s unemployment rate inches upward to 3.8%
rows.standfirst: That’s up from 3.3% in December. The May job report also shows thousands of jobs were added last month.

rows.title: Coloradans who’ve fallen behind on rent can apply for assistance this week as state aims to stem evictions

rows.title: Chaos or success? Questions continue around abrupt closure of U.S. 50 over Blue Mesa.
rows.standfirst: State and federal officials have known for decades about problems with bridges constructed with a faulty welding technique

rows.title: $75 million in federal funds flow into Colorado Springs to expand computer chip manufacturing
rows.standfirst: Entegris, which makes cases for silicon chips, picked the city because of CHIPS Act incentives. Construction is underway on a 130,000-square-foot facility that was once home to a Hewlett Packard plant.

rows.title: Kansas forced Colorado to stop irrigating 25,000 acres of farmland. Was it too soon to put them in the same room?

rows.title: Most Colorado oil and gas wells do not generate enough cash to ensure they will be cleaned up, study says
rows.standfirst: Only a handful of basins in the state have wells profitable enough to cover the cost of remediation, leaving 27,000 wells at risk, a Carbon Tracker analysis finds.

rows.title: Xcel says it needs $1.9 billion to prevent future wildfires as it faces nearly 300 lawsuits over Marshall fire
